# The Belgrade files are not in this repository, and why

The Belgrade processed data are **not redistributed here**. This is a rights position, not a
preference, and not a reluctance to share.

The Belgrade occupancy records were obtained from the city parking authority
(JKP Parking servis Beograd). We hold no written authority to redistribute them. An earlier version
of this repository declared them CC0; that dedication asserted a right we cannot evidence, so it was
withdrawn. A formal request for redistribution permission was sent to the operator on **2026-03**
under Serbia's Law on Free Access to Information of Public Importance. **If and when permission
arrives, these files will be added in a new release of this repository and a new archived version,
and the citation DOI resolves to the newest version automatically.** If permission is refused, that
outcome will be stated here.

The **Birmingham** data are public and are included in full, so the pipeline can be reproduced
end to end by a third party on that city without any request to anyone.

## What you can still verify without the Belgrade files

* Every **result** we obtained is here, in `05_results/reference/` — including all Belgrade
  per-facility outputs. You can inspect, re-aggregate and check every number in the article against
  them.
* Every **script** is here. Nothing about the method is withheld.
* `03_code/verify.py` checks each regenerated table against `05_results/reference/`.

## What you cannot do without them

Re-fit the Belgrade models from processed data. Third-party end-to-end reproduction is therefore
demonstrable **on Birmingham only**. We state this plainly rather than leave it to be discovered.

## How to obtain the data, and how to confirm you have OUR file

Request the parking-occupancy records for the Belgrade public car parks, 4–21 March 2017, from
JKP Parking servis Beograd. The same data family is used in the published parking-allocation
literature (Mladenović et al., *J. Heuristics* 26:377–399, 2020; *Comput. Oper. Res.* 125:105080,
2021), which is a useful precedent to cite in a request.

Rebuild the processed tables with the preprocessing and feature scripts in `03_code/src/`, then
compare against the SHA-256 values below. **If your hashes match these, you have exactly the files
the article was computed from**, and every downstream step will reproduce.

| withheld file | bytes | SHA-256 |

| `belgrade_features.parquet` | 3,214,825 | `aac686419349d1ef819b0924231779ee8c01539370e41217a66b0d36ca2fe43e` |
| `belgrade_features_v2.parquet` | 3,477,600 | `5f93c18730f3eeec70b393f72b657ed5218218d935e67033709c5a723c9c26d0` |
